The Regional Open Space Plan was developed over a two year period and included extensive review by technical experts, public officials and citizens of the region. The Open Space Plan is an implementing element of the Comprehensive General Plan for Northeastern Illinois and it amplifies the development goals and policies that comprise the Comprehensive Plan. This plan was adopted by the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission on March 8, 1971.
There are no large scale recreational or park facilities immediately adjacent to Lincoln Highway. However, there is a Forest Preserve located at the corner of Chicago Road and Lincoln Highway, extending westward to include the western bank of Thorn Creek.
Existing right-of-way, in the area of the Forest Preserve, is sufficient to construct the proposed improvement in that the same roadway section used in the recent improvement of Lincoln Highway adjacent to this project on the east will be continued. This section provides a 14-foot median and four ll-foot traffic lanes. The proposed improvement utilizes this section from the eastern terminus at Aberdeen Street through the Thorn Creek bridge and then tapers to a 16-foot median and 12-foot traffic lanes at Edgewood Avenue. This design will require no additional right-of-way taking from the Forest Preserve, it will minimize damages to properties on the south side of Lincoln Highway between Thorn Creek and Aberdeen Street, and it will provide a smooth transition between the normal roadway section and the completed improvement to Lincoln Highway which terminates at Aberdeen Street.
Further west there is a small playground next to the Roosevelt School from which some frontage land will be required. The school officials requested that certain conditions be attached to the acquisition of this land in order to lessen the impact. The conditions were accepted by the Illinois Department of Transportation and include the replacement of all sidewalks, provision for the replacement of shrubbery either by actual plantings or by compensation with right-of-way damages, at the school district option, and the replacement of the pedestrian underpass with an overpass.
A plan has also been successfully developed whereby the school district will acquire property currently used for Sunnyside Avenue from the City of Chicago Heights. This property is adjacent to the playground area and will help compensate for the loss of land necessitated by the highway improvement. Sunnyside Avenue will terminate with a cul-de-sac at the northern property line of the school.
